reference.citation: Reiss A, Stricker D (2012), IEEE ISWC (PAMAP2, UCI #231, CC-BY 4.0); Rowlands AV et al. (2018) Med Sci Sports Exerc 50:1323-1332 (intensity gradient); van Hees et al. GGIR (CRAN) g.intensitygradient.
reference.description: computeENMO reproduces GGIR::g.applymetrics ENMO to machine precision on the identical PAMAP2 hand-acc signal (749 epochs), summarizeFreeLiving reproduces the intensity gradient / MVPA minutes / ASTP fragmentation on that GGIR-validated ENMO series, AND the Rowlands intensity gradient is checked against GGIR::g.intensitygradient on the identical ENMO series (GGIR default binning): GGIR independently returns the same gradient (-1.19) and the op matches GGIR to machine precision (max abs diff < 1e-8). Binning note: max ENMO ~1.2 g, so GGIR's [4000,8000) mg catch-all bin is empty (n_epochs_over_4000mg=0) and the two conventions coincide -- agreement is under matched bins.
